newsitem.title: USA: Sears to exit software, add 35mm cameras.
newsitem.headline: Sears to exit software, add 35mm cameras.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co said Friday it would exit the software selling business in its Brand Central departments to make room for more video equipment and to add 35-millimeter cameras and film.
"We did some research that indicated 12 percent of our customers thought we did carry 35-millimeter cameras," said Jan Drummond, a spokeswoman for Hoffman Estates, Illinois-based Sears.

At the same time, software is not a major line of business for the retailer, a fact that helped lead to the decision to phase out the product by mid-year, she said. Drummond would not disclose the company's annual software sales.
Aside from 35-millimeter cameras and film, Sears will also expand its video camera business, offering as many as nine brands of "point-and-shoot" video cameras, Drummond said.
Sears is also looking at expanding its communications offerings, such as cellular phones, and refining its bundling of computer products.
Sears's niche is selling families their first home computer, the spokeswoman said.
Sears shares were up 1-1/2 at 51-3/8 Friday.
